The morning sun rose over the quiet harbor and the fishermen prepared their boats for the long day ahead.
They carried nets, ropes and small barrels of fresh water for the trip to the outer banks.
The wind blew gently from the west and the gulls circled above the masts of the old ships.
Every sailor knew the tides of this coast and every sailor respected the storms of autumn.
When the boats returned at dusk the whole village gathered at the pier to see the catch.
The children ran along the wooden planks while the dogs barked at the swinging lanterns.
The oldest fisherman told stories about the sea and the young people listened with open mouths.
